subject: Mythology
title: Studio Ghibli and Shinto Mythology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Studio Ghibli and Shinto Mythology.

hook.text: Spirited Away won an Oscar by telling a Shinto story about a girl trapped in a bathhouse for the gods.

buildup.text: Director Hayao Miyazaki fills his films with kami, yokai, and the Shinto belief that nature is sacred and alive.

discovery.text: Princess Mononoke depicts the clash between industrial progress and the ancient forest spirits — a core Shinto tension.

twist.text: My Neighbor Totoro features a forest spirit millions associate with Japan, but Miyazaki invented him entirely.

climax.text: Ghibli films taught the world Shinto values without ever using the word 'Shinto' — through beauty, not preaching.

punchline.text: The best missionary for Japanese mythology is an animation studio.

quiz.question: What Shinto theme runs through most Studio Ghibli films?
options: The sacredness of nature and respect for spirits in the natural world
Samurai honor codes and loyalty to authority
